sources.title: Pamela Gutman: Ancient Arakan, doctoral thesis (1976)
sources.note: ANU original chapter, indexed full printed 27 and 48 inspected; all chapters/abstract treated as one work. Historical scripts, Sanskrit/Pali, patronage. Exact traditional regnal dates are superseded by Griffiths 2015 and Islam/Cribb 2022; not adopted.

sources.title: Elisabeth Moore: Dhanyawadi and Vesali, Il Mondo dell’Archeologia (2005)
sources.note: Original archaeologist-authored entries directly checked. Dhanyawadi mid-fourth to early sixth century; Vesali coordinates 20°40 N, 93°09 E and excavated ordination hall 21 by 15 m. Related articles on same page pooled. Sectarian blanket claims not adopted.

sources.title: Bob Hudson: Ancient geography and recent archaeology, Dhanyawadi, Vesali and Mrauk-u (2005)
sources.note: Full author-uploaded original paper directly read, pages 1 to 3. Field survey, agricultural geography, walls/gates. Specific calibrated gatepost range 1260 to 1400 CE at 95.4 percent; abstract calling it thirteenth century is less precise. No claim this late gate dates the entire city.

sources.title: Mya Oo: Khraung-kaik Pitaka-taik, historical introduction (2017)
sources.note: ISEAS book chapter, Bagan and the World pp45 to 56, publisher original extract directly read. Introduction says Dhanyawadi archaeology begins in first century CE but supplies no dated excavation context there. Contrast explicitly with Moore; not used to certify BCE kingdom.

sources.title: E. H. Johnston: Some Sanskrit Inscriptions of Arakan (1944)
sources.note: Original scan indexed full passages read, printed 368 and 382: partly mythical earlier king list; verses57 to 65 public works, wells, diplomatic gifts and daughter Dhenda; bell inscription and translation. Original PDF opened but no OCR; exact indexed original and full scholarly transcription mirror cross-checked. Early dating and exclusive sect identification not adopted.

sources.title: Arlo Griffiths: Three More Sanskrit Inscriptions of Arakan (2015)
sources.note: Journal of Burma Studies19.2 pp281 to 340, university abstract and full original article in Scribd mirror read. All versions pooled. Prine Cha A.2 pp294 to 298: exact śākabhājanatrayaṁ and translation, laundry conjecture, slave/buffaloes, king’s elder brother. Pp331 to 332 place A.2/Anandacandra eighth century earliest, possibly ninth; firm absolute dates rejected.

sources.title: Md Shariful Islam and Joe Cribb: Re-reading a Silver Coin of Ancient Arakan (2022)
sources.note: Original scholarly society PDF directly read, printed8 to 14. Hsindet hoard1985 with Arakan and two Pyu coins at printed10 to 11; alternate dynasty chronology and limits at12 to 14. No exact reign years inferred from old table.

sources.title: British Museum: Niticandra silver coin, 1884,0510.1
sources.note: Museum catalogue directly read: 32 mm,7.41g, bull wearing garland, reverse described as trisula with sun/moon. Catalogue dates499 to 554 follow older chronology; public wording explicitly identifies this as catalogue dating and separate research questions dynasty chronology.

sources.title: Department of Archaeology and National Museum: Anandacandra stone inscription nomination (2018)
sources.note: Full official MOWCAP nomination directly read, sections3.2 to 3.4. Use physical pillar, three phases of writing, local history of movement and poor condition. Historical reconstruction contains errors and disputed chronology, so not treated as modern critical edition. No ethnic inference or BCE timeline adopted.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: Exact imported records verified. Earliest arakan gets distinct evidence-limits narrative; 600/900 share a regional urban/epigraphic narrative with explicit phases, not one polity or ethnicity. No Mrauk U aliases changed.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: arakan(-200 to 200) and arakan-600(600 to 700) bbox91.572316E20.349482N93.113131E23.114431N; arakan-900 bbox91.651517E18.953183N94.178742E23.786314N. Point-in-polygon: Dhanyawadi within all; Vesali excluded by first two but included by900. Public warning; no border repair invented.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Griffiths2015 critiques precise729CE dating and sequential king-list assumptions. Prine Cha/Anandacandra eighth century at earliest, ninth possible. Islam/Cribb2022 argues later dynasty dates. Museum499 to 554 labelled catalogue estimate, not accepted exact reign.
batchIdentityNotes.depthException: Earliest record has eight substantive evidence/identity passages, not twelve padded backward projections. Contemporary households/writing remain unverified; later comparisons are explicit. This exception should be reviewed by root, not reported as an equally rich secure polity narrative.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Later card quotes exact scholarly transliteration śākabhājanatrayaṁ, three vegetable platters, PrineChaA.2line9, Griffiths296 to 298. Original script identified but no modern Unicode substitution for ancient glyphs. Earliest card transparently lacks a verified contemporary sample.
batchIdentityNotes.reuse: All works pooled across two drafts; nine distinct new works. No sources from preceding Mrauk U/1783 cards reused. Shared alias prose counted once; both override summaries counted.
